- scripts/security_audit.sh:595-609 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, x-ai_grok-4_6]
  PROBLEM: The prior-findings preprocessor accepts non-canonical repository-relative paths containing interior `..` segments or leading `./`, causing the normalized path to diverge from the path added to the delta-audit scope.
  WHY: Git emits canonical paths and `normalize_finding()` rejects paths containing `..`, so re-emitted prior findings can be silently dropped or fail closed; severity is elevated to critical because one reviewer rated it BLOCKER while the others rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:143-157 | severity=low | confidence=5

  PROBLEM: Previously reported finding text is concatenated into the model prompt without untrusted-content delimiters.
  WHY: Persisted model-generated `exploit_scenario` and `recommendation` text can be interpreted as instructions rather than data.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:548-558 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: Delta narrowing does not validate that `SECURITY_AUDIT_DIFF_BASE` is an ancestor of `SECURITY_AUDIT_DIFF_HEAD`.
  WHY: An inverted or unrelated commit range can produce an incorrect changed-file set and meaningless audit results; severity is elevated to high because one reviewer rated it MAJOR while the other rated it NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5353-5361 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: When prior-findings export fails, the code continues with an empty file path after setting the count to zero without clearly documenting the fallback behavior.
  WHY: The audit intentionally runs without prior-findings memory, but the implicit fallback makes the failure harder to diagnose.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:200-212 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: Delta re-audit prompt-context generation does not explicitly handle a zero-file delta intersection.
  WHY: The model may receive confusing scope information when no files changed since the last audited commit.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5370-5387 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: Resetting security-pass state does not reset `security_pass_cycle` to zero.
  WHY: The cycle counter may no longer represent the number of completed fix cycles after `/re-security-pass`.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5333-5345 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The consolidated fix-issue instruction uses the ambiguous phrase "defect class".
  WHY: Implementers may misinterpret the requested scope and fail to fix every instance of the vulnerability pattern.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:143-157 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The prior-findings prompt says that earlier findings' fixes "have merged into the audited head".
  WHY: This can misrepresent the re-audit state and confuse implementers about whether fixes have already been validated.

  WHY: `normalize_finding()` rejects any path where `".." in candidate_path.parts`, while the preprocessor can append a non-canonical path that never matches canonical paths from git, silently dropping the prior finding from scope.

  WHY: Persisted finding descriptions could influence model behavior during re-audit because the prior-findings block lacks the explicit fencing used for the project-specification block.
